A change to that file after the freeze is an unlock of BOTH tickets: FROZEN_UNLOCK opens one manifest only (.claude/hooks/frozen-manifest.sh: '[ "${FROZEN_UNLOCK:-}" = "$issue" ] && exit 0'), and the hook stop-tests reports the file against the old hash of the other manifest until that one is unlocked and re-hashed too; both test files then run again and both red runs are re-recorded.

1.interface: Target and confirmation (C-Q3): `make docker-clean` reports; `make docker-clean CONFIRM=1`, on the command line or exported in the environment, reports and removes; every other value of CONFIRM is no confirmation. Owner only: the target depends on `owner-session`, so it refuses when CLAUDECODE is set, with that target's message, before any docker call; `make -n docker-clean` exits 0 and calls docker not at all (no `$(shell docker ...)`). If the target has a script it is scripts/docker-clean.sh and no other file, and the script itself refuses when CLAUDECODE is set, before its first docker call (the hook owner-stack does not know the target, so `CONFIRM=1 sh scripts/docker-clean.sh` could otherwise run in a session). One `## ` help line. Throwaway project: a name that matches the rule of ci-guard, `lfc-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*` anchored at both ends, not `lfc-owner`, and not on the fixed exclusion list (C-Q9): `lfc-eval`, `lfc-test` (exact names: lfc-test-1 and lfc-eval-2 are throwaway projects like any other), every name that starts with `lfc-toolbox`, `lfc-agent` or `lfc-probe`. A project has a container when `docker ps -a` shows one with its project label, in any state. Which references belong to a project (C-Q5): a tag that names it, `<registry>/<service>:<project>` with the registry `lfc` or `lfc.invalid` (the name #166 Task 1 gives it, E-F4 and P1) or `<project>-<service>[:tag]`, with or without the label; and an untagged image that carries its label. A tagged image with the project's label loses ONLY the references that name the project, never its other tags and never the image by id: the owner's machine holds one image id with the tags `lfc/detection:local` and `lfc/detection:lfc-25-acc` and the label of lfc-25-acc, and after #166 the same can happen under `lfc.invalid`. Report (stdout, wording free otherwise): only images of throwaway projects, not every image on the machine, and of an image with several tags only the references that name the project; each such reference on one line with the size `docker image ls` prints for it; the lines that name a project differ when it has a container and when it has none, the lines of other projects do not; an excluded project is named as a word of its own on a line with the word `bleibt`, a project that would be cleared never; the size of the build cache as Docker prints it. With CONFIRM=1: the references of the projects without a container go by reference, an untagged image by id, never with `-f`; an image Docker refuses because a container outside the project still uses it stays and the run still exits 0 (C-Q11); the build cache records older than 168 hours go (C-Q4; `docker builder prune -f --filter until=168h`). Exit 0 when nothing is to remove (Docker fails on `image rm` without an argument). Never: an image of a project with a container, of an excluded project, of a project outside the rule (lfc-owner, live-factchecker-v2, live-factcheck, lab-*, docker-*-mcp-*, lfc-_tmp, xlfc-1, lfcx-1, lfc), an image without label and project tag (third-party, minikube), a volume, a container, `compose down`, `system prune`, `image prune` without a label filter (and not with one either: it takes the whole image with every tag).
1.note: The tests run make in a throwaway copy (Makefile, *.mk, .nvmrc, scripts/, compose*.yml) with tools/tests/fake_docker.py as `docker` on a PATH of the fake and /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin only (the host needs Docker, Git and make; no jq, no Homebrew tool), stdin is empty. The fake models a fixed set of docker calls (its header lists them); a call outside that set exits 64 and fails the case, so stay inside the list or report BLOCKED. Each fake call costs about 50 ms: with one `docker image inspect` per image the file runs about 50 s; fewer calls per run keep `make ci-local` short. Read the containers of a project again directly before removing its references: between the report and the removal a stack may have started; without `-f` Docker refuses an image in use, which is the second line of defence. Not specified by the ticket and not asserted: the exit code when a removal fails for another reason than an image in use, a second report after the removal, an image whose label and tag name two different throwaway projects (leave it).
1.fake: Where the fake decides and the real Docker may differ (header of tools/tests/fake_docker.py, last paragraph). (1) tools/tests/fake_docker.py:381 ('gone = [r for r in state["cache"] if all(r["hours"] > limit for limit in limits)]'): `docker builder prune` without `-a` removes every record older than the filter there; whether the real BuildKit needs `--all` to reach the records that fill the disk is for the owner's real run (ticket: 'The real run is the owner's (the target refuses for agents): one report before and after, pasted into the ticket'). (2) The fake is static: no race between listing and removing. (3) tools/tests/fake_docker.py:463-464: `compose down --rmi` exits 1 on a failed removal; not used by this ticket (compose down is forbidden here). Changed in round 2: `image ls -q` prints one id per tag line, as Docker does (an id with two tags shows twice; `sort -u` before a loop over ids). `image rm -f` of an image that only stopped containers use: in the fake the tag goes and the image stays untagged; what the real Docker does depends on its image store (the classic store removes the image, containerd keeps it untagged) and is not proven. The tag is gone either way, the cases do not depend on which of the two happens, and no real run shows it, because `-f` is forbidden.
